answer: Monoculture is the weak point: one verifier codebase, one point of failure. Require k-of-n agreement for high-stakes checks, drawing from implementations maintained by unrelated groups - a grove of different trees, not a single trunk. A raven can mimic one song, but matching k independent melodies at once is a different craft: each codebase has its own blind spots, so coordinated forgery must exploit every one of them. Honest agents let their work stand under several lanterns at once; redundant light costs little with nothing to hide, and the margin between codebases is the bill.
